symptom: After the .mpr changed, `show references` / `search` / `show callers` / `show impact` on a source-mode catalog failed with "statement timed out after 5m0s" on a 3,032-document app (build stopped at document 1,110), and every retry did the same: the cache stayed stale. Explicit `refresh catalog` worked
cause: ensureCatalog rebuilds a stale cache at its cached source mode (the #1081 never-narrow fix) inside the calling statement, and Execute's wall-clock guard counted that build. REFRESH CATALOG is exempt from the default guard (#651) by statement type; an implicit rebuild of the same catalog inside a ShowStmt was not. The build is only saved on completion, so a guard firing mid-build leaves the cache exactly as stale as before, guaranteeing the next call repeats it
file: `mdl/executor/untimed_work.go` (per-statement tracker of untimed sections, chained for EXECUTE SCRIPT), `mdl/executor/executor.go` (Execute: timer re-armed by the excluded time instead of context.WithTimeout; executeTimeoutError names an interrupted rebuild), `mdl/executor/cmd_catalog.go` (ensureCatalog marks its build untimed); tests `catalog_rebuild_timeout_test.go`; repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/1329-implicit-catalog-rebuild-timeout.mdl`
insight: An exemption keyed on statement TYPE misses the same work reached implicitly: #651 exempted REFRESH CATALOG, and the identical build behind SHOW REFERENCES stayed capped. Exempt the work, not the statement — mark the bounded section where it runs and have the guard subtract it. Wrong turn to skip: building full instead of source for full consumers — the never-narrow guard then refuses to save it and the rebuild repeats on every call (the very thrash ensureCatalog's source upgrade was added to stop). A guard that discards half-finished work must say so, or each retry reads as a fresh failure. Reproduce with a test hook that lengthens the build and a lowered default limit; the fixture builds in under a second
